Benchmark the local LLMs you already have — speed, memory, energy, and quality — as a live terminal leaderboard.

local_bench is a single-command TUI that discovers the models installed in your local runner (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, or any OpenAI-compatible server), runs a curated quality suite, measures tokens/sec, time-to-first-token, memory footprint, and optionally joules per token on your actual machine, and renders a live comparison leaderboard.

git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git
cd local_bench
pip install .
local_bench

That's it. No config, no API keys, no cloud.

Why

There are great tools for one half of this problem, but nothing local-first that does both:

  • llama-bench (inside llama.cpp) measures speed only.
  • lm-evaluation-harness measures quality but has no polished laptop UX and isn't built around the model runners most people actually use locally.

local_bench fills the gap: local-first, zero-config, UX-driven. Clone-and-run, point it at the models you already pulled, and get an at-a-glance answer to "which of my local models is actually good, and how fast is it on this laptop?"

What it measures

Metric How
tok/s Output tokens ÷ generation time. Ollama reports server-side eval timing; OpenAI-compatible backends are timed client-side from the token stream. Excludes prompt processing and model load.
TTFT Wall-clock time to the first streamed token (minus model-load time where the runner reports it).
Memory Resident model size when the runner exposes it (Ollama /api/ps, LM Studio /api/v0), plus a best-effort peak-RSS sample of the backend's processes.
Energy Joules per output token, with --energy. Sampled from the platform power meter (macOS powermetrics, Linux RAPL) during the speed probe, minus an idle baseline measured once per run. Needs root — see Energy.
Quality 31 deterministically-graded tasks across math, reasoning, factual recall, instruction-following/structured-output, extraction, and code understanding. Optional LLM-as-judge adds open-ended tasks (summaries, email, haiku, explanations).

Install

Not published to a package index — install from a clone:

git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git
cd local_bench
pip install .                  # then run:  local_bench

Prefer to keep it isolated? Create a virtualenv first, or install with pipx from the same directory:

pipx install .

Optional extras (all installed the same way, from the clone):

Extra Adds
pip install '.[yaml]' YAML task packs (JSON packs work without it)
pip install '.[anthropic]' the anthropic provider, for Claude as the judge
pip install -e '.[dev]' editable install plus the test dependencies

Requires Python 3.9+.

Usage

local_bench                        # fast default: 3 smallest models, quick suite (TUI)
local_bench --all                  # benchmark every discovered model
local_bench --full                 # run the full quality suite (not just the fast subset)
local_bench --no-tui               # plain live renderer (great for piping / CI)
local_bench -m llama3.2,qwen3:8b   # only these models
local_bench --limit 3              # cap the number of models
local_bench --provider lmstudio    # use LM Studio instead of auto-detect
local_bench --provider llamacpp    # llama.cpp server (llama-server)
local_bench --provider vllm        # vLLM
local_bench --provider openai --host http://localhost:5000   # any OpenAI-compatible server
local_bench --refresh-cache        # recompute instead of reusing cached responses
local_bench --energy               # also measure joules per token (see Energy)
local_bench --no-quality           # speed + memory only (fast)
local_bench --no-speed             # quality only
local_bench --judge qwen3:8b       # enable LLM-as-judge (adds open-ended tasks)
local_bench --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://gateway  # judge off-box
local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml    # use a custom task pack instead of the built-in suite
local_bench --only math            # run one category, or name task ids
local_bench --num-ctx 16384        # raise the context window (needed for long prompts)
local_bench --add-tasks mypack.yaml  # add a pack on top of the built-in suite
local_bench --label "before tuning"  # tag this run for later diffing
local_bench --md results.md        # also export a Markdown report
local_bench --json results.json    # also export raw JSON

local_bench list                   # just list discovered models
local_bench tasks                  # show the quality suite (add --tasks to preview a pack)
local_bench history                # list past runs (saved automatically)
local_bench diff                   # diff the two most recent runs
local_bench diff 3 1               # diff run #3 (base) against run #1 (newer)
local_bench throughput             # batch-throughput sweep (concurrency 1,2,4,8)
local_bench throughput --concurrency 1,8,16 --provider vllm
local_bench fit                    # which popular models fit YOUR hardware?

Run local_bench --help for the full flag list.

Avg task is the mean wall-clock time to complete one quality task. It covers only tasks that were actually generated — a cached response does no work, so a fully cached run shows – rather than a near-zero time it never measured. With --energy, a J/tok column joins the board.

(Numbers are for that laptop at that moment — see Limitations.)

Providers

At least one local model runner must be reachable:

Provider --provider Default host Host env var Notes
Ollama ollama http://localhost:11434 OLLAMA_HOST Native API; reports model memory via /api/ps.
LM Studio lmstudio http://localhost:1234 LMSTUDIO_HOST Enriches metadata + memory via native /api/v0.
llama.cpp llamacpp http://localhost:8080 LLAMACPP_HOST llama-server, OpenAI-compatible.
vLLM vllm http://localhost:8000 VLLM_HOST Set VLLM_API_KEY if started with --api-key.
OpenAI-compatible openai — OPENAI_BASE_URL Any /v1 server (Jan, LocalAI, TGI, …); pass --host.
Anthropic (Claude) anthropic api.anthropic.com ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Hosted, not local — intended for --judge-provider anthropic. Needs pip install '.[anthropic]'.

Auto-detection tries Ollama → LM Studio → llama.cpp → vLLM (the generic openai provider is explicit-only). Force one with --provider. Override host with --host or the env var above.

How quality grading works

The suite is small on purpose — enough tasks across categories to separate models, few enough that every model runs in a couple of minutes on a laptop. Each task is graded deterministically (exact numeric match, multiple-choice letter, substring, valid-JSON, regex). Temperature is 0 and a fixed seed is used for reproducibility. See local_bench tasks for the list.

The optional --judge MODEL flag turns on an LLM-as-judge (any local model) that scores open-ended tasks 1–5 against a reference answer. It's a signal, not an oracle.

Fast by default

Benchmarking every model on the full suite takes a while on a laptop, so the defaults are tuned for a quick first look:

  • 3 smallest models by default (smallest first, so results appear fast) — --all for everything, -m to choose.
  • A fast quality subset (~8 tasks across all categories) — --full for all 31.
  • Response caching: quality runs use temperature 0 + a fixed seed, so responses are deterministic and cached under ~/.local_bench. Re-running only regenerates new models/tasks (unchanged ones are re-graded from cache in milliseconds); --refresh-cache forces recompute, --no-cache disables it.

In practice this turns a first run from ~15–25 min (all models, full suite) into ~1–2 min, and a re-run into seconds. For a thorough pass (CI, final numbers) use local_bench --all --full.

Custom task packs

Bring your own evals with a JSON or YAML pack — no Python required. --tasks replaces the built-in suite; --add-tasks appends to it. YAML needs the optional extra (pip install ".[yaml]"); JSON works out of the box.

# mypack.yaml  —  local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml
name: my-pack
tasks:
  - id: capital_japan
    category: factual
    prompt: "What is the capital of Japan? Answer with just the city name."
    grader: {type: contains_any, values: ["Tokyo"]}
    reference: Tokyo
  - id: add
    category: math
    prompt: "What is 12 + 30? End with the answer on its own line."
    grader: {type: exact_number, value: 42}
  - id: explain          # no grader -> open-ended, scored only with --judge
    category: open
    prompt: "Explain photosynthesis in one sentence."
    reference: "Plants convert sunlight, water, and CO2 into glucose and oxygen."

Grader type values: exact_number (value, tol), multiple_choice (value), contains_any (values), regex (pattern, ignorecase), valid_json (keys), valid_json_array (length). Omit grader for a judge-only task. Preview any pack with local_bench tasks --tasks mypack.yaml.

Two runnable packs ship in examples/: sample_pack.yaml is a four-task look at the format, and extended_pack.yaml is a 21-task template covering every category and every grader type — copy it and swap in your own prompts.

Two rules keep a pack honest, both enforced by the tests for the shipped ones:

  • Every deterministic task's reference must pass its own grader. The reference is the worked example of a correct answer; if it can't clear the grader, nothing can, and the resulting 0 looks like a model failure rather than an authoring one.
  • max_tokens must have headroom. The budget covers the whole reply. With exact_number — which reads the last number — a model that reaches the right answer and then keeps talking gets cut off mid-sentence and scored on whatever number landed last. Ask for the answer last, and say to stop there.

Reviewing a pack before you run it

local_bench tasks --tasks mypack.yaml prints a pack to the terminal. For a bigger one there's also a small browser UI, tools/pack_viewer, which shows every task next to the exact grader spec that will judge it, charts prompt sizes against the context window the model will actually be loaded with, and applies both rules above to your pack — re-grading each reference with its own grader, and flagging prompts that will overflow the context:

pip install -r tools/pack_viewer/requirements.txt
streamlit run tools/pack_viewer/app.py -- mypack.yaml

A standalone utility rather than part of the package: nothing in src/ imports it, and Streamlit stays out of local_bench's own dependencies.

Judging with a different provider

By default the judge runs on the same provider as the models under test, so it can only be a model that provider serves. On one local runner that usually means the judge is also a candidate — and then it scores its own answers on the open-ended tasks. --judge-provider and --judge-host point the judge somewhere else:

local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml \
  --judge <model-your-gateway-serves> \
  --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://your-gateway

openai is the wire protocol, not the vendor. Any OpenAI-compatible gateway works — LiteLLM, vLLM, Jan, LocalAI, TGI — and the judge is whatever model you pass to --judge, from any provider behind it. This is the way to grade small local models with a capable hosted one.

Claude as the judge

Anthropic's API is not OpenAI-compatible — there is no /v1/chat/completions on api.anthropic.com — so --judge-provider openai cannot reach it directly. Use the dedicated provider, which talks to the Messages API through the official SDK:

pip install '.[anthropic]'
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-…

local_bench --judge claude-opus-5 --judge-provider anthropic

--judge takes any Claude model id (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5); Opus is the strongest and the usual reason to send the judge off-box. Three request parameters have no Anthropic equivalent and are handled rather than passed through: temperature is rejected by current Claude models so it is dropped (and response caching switches off for this backend, since determinism can't be promised), --num-ctx is fixed server-side and is reported as ignored, and thinking is disabled unless you pass --think — left on, it would spend the judge's small token budget reasoning and return no score.

You can still route Claude through a gateway with --judge-provider openai --judge-host … if you already run one; the difference is that the anthropic provider needs no gateway.

API keys

Keys are read from the environment, and the variable does not have to carry a vendor's name:

Order Variable
1 whatever you name with --judge-api-key-env (or --api-key-env for the models under test)
2 $LOCAL_BENCH_JUDGE_API_KEY / $LOCAL_BENCH_API_KEY
3 the provider's own (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, VLLM_API_KEY, …)

For the Anthropic provider, an unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY does not necessarily mean no credentials: with none of the above set, the SDK falls back to ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and then to a profile from ant auth login.

LITELLM_KEY=sk-… local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml --judge <model> \
  --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://litellm.internal \
  --judge-api-key-env LITELLM_KEY

local_bench warns if the judge is also one of the benchmarked models, and errors rather than proceeding if the judge endpoint is unreachable — an unreachable judge would score every open-ended task 0, which looks identical to uniformly bad writing.

Long prompts: set --num-ctx

If your pack has long prompts — a multi-file diff, a transcript, a log — raise the context window, or you may be grading truncation instead of the model:

local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml --num-ctx 16384

Ollama loads a model at 4096 tokens by default, no matter what the model itself supports (Gemma 3 advertises 131072 and still loads at 4096). A prompt past that is not rejected and does not error — Ollama discards the older half of the context and evaluates the rest. Measured on 0.32.3: a 4,450-token prompt reported prompt_eval_count=2051, and everything stated at the top of the prompt was gone, so the model answered confidently from a fragment. The grader just records a wrong answer, and nothing in the results says the prompt never arrived.

local_bench warns before a run when a task's prompt + max_tokens looks likely to overflow that default, but it can only estimate token counts, so set --num-ctx explicitly when you know your prompts are long. Note the trade-off: a larger context reserves more KV cache, which counts against the memory a model needs — so size it to your prompts rather than maximizing it.

--num-ctx applies to Ollama only. OpenAI-compatible servers fix their context at startup (llama.cpp --ctx-size, vLLM --max-model-len); local_bench warns if you pass it to one of those.

History & diffing

Every run is saved automatically to $LOCAL_BENCH_HOME/runs (default ~/.local_bench/runs); disable with --no-save, and tag runs with --label.

local_bench history            # table of past runs (newest first)
local_bench diff               # previous run -> latest
local_bench diff 3             # run #3 -> latest
local_bench diff 3 1           # run #3 (base) -> run #1 (newer)

diff compares models by name and shows per-model deltas in quality and throughput, plus which models were added or removed between runs — handy for "did that quantization / setting actually help?"

Batch throughput

The main leaderboard measures single-stream tok/s. Servers that batch requests (vLLM, llama.cpp continuous batching, Ollama with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL>1) can do far more total work under concurrency — local_bench throughput measures that:

local_bench throughput -m my-model --concurrency 1,2,4,8

It fires N requests at each concurrency level (N defaults to 3×concurrency) and reports aggregate tok/s (total output ÷ wall-clock), the speedup vs. concurrency 1, mean per-request rate, and latency (mean / p95):

│    1 │    4 │      95.0 │   1.00× │      95.0 │   1.35 s │  1.4 s  │      0 │
│    4 │   12 │     320.0 │   3.37× │      82.0 │   1.56 s │  1.9 s  │      0 │
│    8 │   24 │     540.0 │   5.68× │      70.0 │   1.83 s │  2.6 s  │      0 │
└──────┴──────┴───────────┴─────────┴───────────┴──────────┴─────────┴────────┘

On a non-batching setup, aggregate throughput stays flat while latency climbs — which is itself a useful thing to see. Add --json FILE to export.

What can my machine run?

Before benchmarking, local_bench fit captures your hardware (RAM, CPU, GPU/VRAM, Apple unified memory) and checks a catalog of ~50 popular models — SmolLM2, Qwen2.5, Llama 3.x, Gemma 2, Phi-3.5/4, Mistral/Mixtral, DeepSeek-R1, CodeLlama, Yi, Command-R, and more, from 135M up to 141B — against your memory budget, showing which fit and at what quantization:

local_bench fit                    # what fits, at the best quant
local_bench fit --all              # include models that don't fit
local_bench fit --context 8192     # budget a larger KV cache
local_bench fit --quant Q4_K_M     # evaluate a specific quant
local_bench fit --vram 24          # what-if: "if I had a 24 GB GPU…"
local_bench fit --catalog my.json  # add your own models to the catalog

Live list from HuggingFace

Instead of the built-in catalog, pull the currently most popular models straight from the HuggingFace Hub — their parameter counts (from safetensors metadata) are sized against your hardware in real time:

local_bench fit --online              # top 50 text-generation models by downloads
local_bench fit --online --top 100    # cast a wider net
local_bench fit --online --sort trending   # or: likes
local_bench fit --online --refresh    # bypass the 1-day cache

Results are cached under $LOCAL_BENCH_HOME (~/.local_bench), so repeat runs are fast and work offline; if the Hub is unreachable, local_bench falls back to the cache (or the built-in catalog).

The built-in catalog also ships each model's Ollama tag (ollama pull …) and HuggingFace repo (which LM Studio and vLLM pull from). Add your own with a JSON catalog (see examples/models.example.json): a list of {name, params_b, family?, ollama?, hf?}. Sizes are estimates (weights + KV cache + overhead), so treat "fits"/"tight" as guidance. Add --json FILE to export the hardware profile and results.

Energy

On a laptop, joules per token is often the number that actually decides a model: two models at the same tok/s can differ several-fold in power draw, which is the difference between one you can leave running on battery and one you can't.

local_bench --energy                 # J/token alongside tok/s and quality
local_bench --energy --full --md out.md
Platform Meter Covers
macOS powermetrics CPU + GPU + ANE package
Linux powercap RAPL (/sys/class/powercap) CPU package only

Both meters need root, so --energy is off by default and reports why it is unavailable rather than showing an empty column after a full run.

The recommended setup grants passwordless access to only the power meter, so local_bench itself keeps running as you:

# sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/local_bench
your-username ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/powermetrics

local_bench --energy          # no sudo on local_bench itself

local_bench --energy prints the exact line to add, with your username and the resolved binary path filled in.

Running the whole tool under sudo also works, but whether $HOME is preserved depends on your sudo configuration — so run history and the response cache may land in root's home, or become root-owned files in yours. If you go that route, be explicit:

sudo LOCAL_BENCH_HOME="$HOME/.local_bench" local_bench --energy

How the number is derived. Neither macOS nor Linux exposes per-process energy, so the meters read whole-system power. local_bench measures idle draw once per run and subtracts it, giving a net figure attributable to inference:

joules_net = (mean_watts − baseline_watts) × sampled_seconds
J/token    = joules_net ÷ output_tokens

The Markdown report shows net and gross joules, mean watts, and the baseline that was subtracted, so you can see how much of the total was overhead. Keep the machine otherwise idle for a clean baseline.

Limitations

local_bench is a fast, local first look — not a rigorous benchmark of record. Keep these in mind:

  • Quality is a signal, not a leaderboard of record. The suite is small and English-only (8 tasks in the fast default, 31 with --full); it's designed to separate your models, not to rank them authoritatively. For serious evals use lm-evaluation-harness. The optional LLM-as-judge is noisy, especially with small local judges.
  • Speed is your-machine-at-that-moment. tok/s and TTFT depend on current load, thermal state, and memory pressure — a busy laptop (or swapping when low on RAM) will read slower. Numbers are meaningful relative to each other on the same run, not as absolute model specs.
  • Memory is best-effort. It uses the runner's resident size where exposed (Ollama /api/ps, LM Studio /api/v0) plus RSS sampling; on unified-memory Macs it's approximate, and client-timed for OpenAI-compatible backends.
  • fit sizes are estimates (weights + KV cache + overhead) — treat "fits/tight" as guidance, not a guarantee. HuggingFace param counts come from safetensors metadata, which is missing for GGUF-only or gated repos.
  • Throughput scaling only appears on batching servers (vLLM, etc.); a single local model serializes requests.
  • Energy is a whole-system estimate. The platform meters measure the machine, not the process, and Apple documents powermetrics values as model-derived estimates that "should not be used for any comparison between devices". Subtracting the idle baseline makes the numbers comparable between models in one run on one machine — nothing more. Anything else running during the probe lands in the reading, and on Linux, RAPL sees the CPU package only, so a discrete GPU's draw is missing entirely.
  • Response caching needs a model version. Ollama reports a content digest and LM Studio reports file size and quantization, so cached answers can be tied to exact weights. A bare OpenAI-compatible endpoint reports only a model name, so those models are re-generated every run rather than risk scoring one model against another's cached answers.

Development

git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git
cd local_bench
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q

The repo ships a pre-commit config that runs gitleaks plus a few hygiene hooks, so a secret is caught before it reaches history rather than in CI after it's already there:

pip install pre-commit    # or: brew install pre-commit
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files   # optional: check the existing tree

The codebase is small and layered: providers/ (pluggable backends), quality/ (tasks, graders, judge), metrics/ (memory sampling), runner.py (orchestration), report.py (export + tables), and tui/ + plainui.py (rendering). Adding a provider means subclassing Provider (or OpenAICompatibleProvider) and registering it; adding a task means appending to the suite in quality/tasks.py with a reference that satisfies its grader (enforced by the tests).

Outside the package, tools/ holds standalone developer utilities — currently the pack viewer. They may import local_bench, never the reverse, and their dependencies are their own, so they can't weigh down an install of the CLI.

Contributions welcome — new providers, task packs, and metrics especially.

Roadmap

  • Energy per token (--energy)
  • Re-record the terminal demo casts under the local_bench name (the originals were removed with the fork)

  • Per-run environment capture (OS, RAM, GPU) for comparable results

Install Not published to a package index — install from a clone: git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git cd local_bench pip install . # then run: local_bench Prefer to keep it isolated? Create a virtualenv first, or install with pipx from the same directory: pipx install . Optional extras (all installed the same way, from the clone): Extra Adds pip install '.[yaml]' YAML task packs (JSON packs work without it) pip install '.[anthropic]' the anthropic provider, for Claude as the judge pip install -e '.[dev]' editable install plus the test dependencies Requires Python 3.9+. Usage local_bench # fast default: 3 smallest models, quick suite (TUI) local_bench --all # benchmark every discovered model local_bench --full # run the full quality suite (not just the fast subset) local_bench --no-tui # plain live renderer (great for piping / CI) local_bench -m llama3.2,qwen3:8b # only these models local_bench --limit 3 # cap the number of models local_bench --provider lmstudio # use LM Studio instead of auto-detect local_bench --provider llamacpp # llama.cpp server (llama-server) local_bench --provider vllm # vLLM local_bench --provider openai --host http://localhost:5000 # any OpenAI-compatible server local_bench --refresh-cache # recompute instead of reusing cached responses local_bench --energy # also measure joules per token (see Energy) local_bench --no-quality # speed + memory only (fast) local_bench --no-speed # quality only local_bench --judge qwen3:8b # enable LLM-as-judge (adds open-ended tasks) local_bench --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://gateway # judge off-box local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml # use a custom task pack instead of the built-in suite local_bench --only math # run one category, or name task ids local_bench --num-ctx 16384 # raise the context window (needed for long prompts) local_bench --add-tasks mypack.yaml # add a pack on top of the built-in suite local_bench --label "before tuning" # tag this run for later diffing local_bench --md results.md # also export a Markdown report local_bench --json results.json # also export raw JSON local_bench list # just list discovered models local_bench tasks # show the quality suite (add --tasks to preview a pack) local_bench history # list past runs (saved automatically) local_bench diff # diff the two most recent runs local_bench diff 3 1 # diff run #3 (base) against run #1 (newer) local_bench throughput # batch-throughput sweep (concurrency 1,2,4,8) local_bench throughput --concurrency 1,8,16 --provider vllm local_bench fit # which popular models fit YOUR hardware? Run local_bench --help for the full flag list. Example output A real quick-suite run on an Apple M4, via Ollama: Final leaderboard ┏━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┓ ┃ # ┃ Model ┃ Params ┃ Quality ┃ Pass ┃ tok/s ┃ TTFT ┃ Avg task ┃ Memory ┃ ┡━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━┩ │ 1 │ gemma4:latest │ 8.0B │ 100% │ 8/8 │ 27.7 │ 205 ms │ 1.29 s │ 8.8 GB │ │ 2 │ gemma3:latest │ 4.3B │ 62% │ 5/8 │ 34.6 │ 160 ms │ 1.23 s │ 3.5 GB │ └───┴───────────────┴────────┴─────────┴──────┴───────┴────────┴──────────┴────────┘ Avg task is the mean wall-clock time to complete one quality task. It covers only tasks that were actually generated — a cached response does no work, so a fully cached run shows – rather than a near-zero time it never measured. With --energy, a J/tok column joins the board. (Numbers are for that laptop at that moment — see Limitations.) Providers At least one local model runner must be reachable: Provider --provider Default host Host env var Notes Ollama ollama http://localhost:11434 OLLAMA_HOST Native API; reports model memory via /api/ps. LM Studio lmstudio http://localhost:1234 LMSTUDIO_HOST Enriches metadata + memory via native /api/v0. llama.cpp llamacpp http://localhost:8080 LLAMACPP_HOST llama-server, OpenAI-compatible. vLLM vllm http://localhost:8000 VLLM_HOST Set VLLM_API_KEY if started with --api-key. OpenAI-compatible openai — OPENAI_BASE_URL Any /v1 server (Jan, LocalAI, TGI, …); pass --host. Anthropic (Claude) anthropic api.anthropic.com ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Hosted, not local — intended for --judge-provider anthropic. Needs pip install '.[anthropic]'. Auto-detection tries Ollama → LM Studio → llama.cpp → vLLM (the generic openai provider is explicit-only). Force one with --provider. Override host with --host or the env var above. How quality grading works The suite is small on purpose — enough tasks across categories to separate models, few enough that every model runs in a couple of minutes on a laptop. Each task is graded deterministically (exact numeric match, multiple-choice letter, substring, valid-JSON, regex). Temperature is 0 and a fixed seed is used for reproducibility. See local_bench tasks for the list. The optional --judge MODEL flag turns on an LLM-as-judge (any local model) that scores open-ended tasks 1–5 against a reference answer. It's a signal, not an oracle. Fast by default Benchmarking every model on the full suite takes a while on a laptop, so the defaults are tuned for a quick first look: 3 smallest models by default (smallest first, so results appear fast) — --all for everything, -m to choose. A fast quality subset (~8 tasks across all categories) — --full for all 31. Response caching: quality runs use temperature 0 + a fixed seed, so responses are deterministic and cached under ~/.local_bench. Re-running only regenerates new models/tasks (unchanged ones are re-graded from cache in milliseconds); --refresh-cache forces recompute, --no-cache disables it. In practice this turns a first run from ~15–25 min (all models, full suite) into ~1–2 min, and a re-run into seconds. For a thorough pass (CI, final numbers) use local_bench --all --full. Custom task packs Bring your own evals with a JSON or YAML pack — no Python required. --tasks replaces the built-in suite; --add-tasks appends to it. YAML needs the optional extra (pip install ".[yaml]"); JSON works out of the box. # mypack.yaml — local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml name: my-pack tasks: - id: capital_japan category: factual prompt: "What is the capital of Japan? Answer with just the city name." grader: {type: contains_any, values: ["Tokyo"]} reference: Tokyo - id: add category: math prompt: "What is 12 + 30? End with the answer on its own line." grader: {type: exact_number, value: 42} - id: explain # no grader -> open-ended, scored only with --judge category: open prompt: "Explain photosynthesis in one sentence." reference: "Plants convert sunlight, water, and CO2 into glucose and oxygen." Grader type values: exact_number (value, tol), multiple_choice (value), contains_any (values), regex (pattern, ignorecase), valid_json (keys), valid_json_array (length). Omit grader for a judge-only task. Preview any pack with local_bench tasks --tasks mypack.yaml. Two runnable packs ship in examples/: sample_pack.yaml is a four-task look at the format, and extended_pack.yaml is a 21-task template covering every category and every grader type — copy it and swap in your own prompts. Two rules keep a pack honest, both enforced by the tests for the shipped ones: Every deterministic task's reference must pass its own grader. The reference is the worked example of a correct answer; if it can't clear the grader, nothing can, and the resulting 0 looks like a model failure rather than an authoring one. max_tokens must have headroom. The budget covers the whole reply. With exact_number — which reads the last number — a model that reaches the right answer and then keeps talking gets cut off mid-sentence and scored on whatever number landed last. Ask for the answer last, and say to stop there. Reviewing a pack before you run it local_bench tasks --tasks mypack.yaml prints a pack to the terminal. For a bigger one there's also a small browser UI, tools/pack_viewer, which shows every task next to the exact grader spec that will judge it, charts prompt sizes against the context window the model will actually be loaded with, and applies both rules above to your pack — re-grading each reference with its own grader, and flagging prompts that will overflow the context: pip install -r tools/pack_viewer/requirements.txt streamlit run tools/pack_viewer/app.py -- mypack.yaml A standalone utility rather than part of the package: nothing in src/ imports it, and Streamlit stays out of local_bench's own dependencies. Judging with a different provider By default the judge runs on the same provider as the models under test, so it can only be a model that provider serves. On one local runner that usually means the judge is also a candidate — and then it scores its own answers on the open-ended tasks. --judge-provider and --judge-host point the judge somewhere else: local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml \ --judge <model-your-gateway-serves> \ --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://your-gateway openai is the wire protocol, not the vendor. Any OpenAI-compatible gateway works — LiteLLM, vLLM, Jan, LocalAI, TGI — and the judge is whatever model you pass to --judge, from any provider behind it. This is the way to grade small local models with a capable hosted one. Claude as the judge Anthropic's API is not OpenAI-compatible — there is no /v1/chat/completions on api.anthropic.com — so --judge-provider openai cannot reach it directly. Use the dedicated provider, which talks to the Messages API through the official SDK: pip install '.[anthropic]' export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-… local_bench --judge claude-opus-5 --judge-provider anthropic --judge takes any Claude model id (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5); Opus is the strongest and the usual reason to send the judge off-box. Three request parameters have no Anthropic equivalent and are handled rather than passed through: temperature is rejected by current Claude models so it is dropped (and response caching switches off for this backend, since determinism can't be promised), --num-ctx is fixed server-side and is reported as ignored, and thinking is disabled unless you pass --think — left on, it would spend the judge's small token budget reasoning and return no score. You can still route Claude through a gateway with --judge-provider openai --judge-host … if you already run one; the difference is that the anthropic provider needs no gateway. API keys Keys are read from the environment, and the variable does not have to carry a vendor's name: Order Variable 1 whatever you name with --judge-api-key-env (or --api-key-env for the models under test) 2 $LOCAL_BENCH_JUDGE_API_KEY / $LOCAL_BENCH_API_KEY 3 the provider's own (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, VLLM_API_KEY, …) For the Anthropic provider, an unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY does not necessarily mean no credentials: with none of the above set, the SDK falls back to ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and then to a profile from ant auth login. LITELLM_KEY=sk-… local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml --judge <model> \ --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://litellm.internal \ --judge-api-key-env LITELLM_KEY local_bench warns if the judge is also one of the benchmarked models, and errors rather than proceeding if the judge endpoint is unreachable — an unreachable judge would score every open-ended task 0, which looks identical to uniformly bad writing. Long prompts: set --num-ctx If your pack has long prompts — a multi-file diff, a transcript, a log — raise the context window, or you may be grading truncation instead of the model: local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml --num-ctx 16384 Ollama loads a model at 4096 tokens by default, no matter what the model itself supports (Gemma 3 advertises 131072 and still loads at 4096). A prompt past that is not rejected and does not error — Ollama discards the older half of the context and evaluates the rest. Measured on 0.32.3: a 4,450-token prompt reported prompt_eval_count=2051, and everything stated at the top of the prompt was gone, so the model answered confidently from a fragment. The grader just records a wrong answer, and nothing in the results says the prompt never arrived. local_bench warns before a run when a task's prompt + max_tokens looks likely to overflow that default, but it can only estimate token counts, so set --num-ctx explicitly when you know your prompts are long. Note the trade-off: a larger context reserves more KV cache, which counts against the memory a model needs — so size it to your prompts rather than maximizing it. --num-ctx applies to Ollama only. OpenAI-compatible servers fix their context at startup (llama.cpp --ctx-size, vLLM --max-model-len); local_bench warns if you pass it to one of those. History & diffing Every run is saved automatically to $LOCAL_BENCH_HOME/runs (default ~/.local_bench/runs); disable with --no-save, and tag runs with --label. local_bench history # table of past runs (newest first) local_bench diff # previous run -> latest local_bench diff 3 # run #3 -> latest local_bench diff 3 1 # run #3 (base) -> run #1 (newer) diff compares models by name and shows per-model deltas in quality and throughput, plus which models were added or removed between runs — handy for "did that quantization / setting actually help?" Batch throughput The main leaderboard measures single-stream tok/s. Servers that batch requests (vLLM, llama.cpp continuous batching, Ollama with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL>1) can do far more total work under concurrency — local_bench throughput measures that: local_bench throughput -m my-model --concurrency 1,2,4,8 It fires N requests at each concurrency level (N defaults to 3×concurrency) and reports aggregate tok/s (total output ÷ wall-clock), the speedup vs. concurrency 1, mean per-request rate, and latency (mean / p95): Batch throughput — my-model (vllm) ┏━━━━━━┳━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┓ ┃ Conc ┃ Reqs ┃ Agg tok/s ┃ Speedup ┃ Req tok/s ┃ Mean lat ┃ p95 lat ┃ Errors ┃ ┡━━━━━━╇━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━┩ │ 1 │ 4 │ 95.0 │ 1.00× │ 95.0 │ 1.35 s │ 1.4 s │ 0 │ │ 4 │ 12 │ 320.0 │ 3.37× │ 82.0 │ 1.56 s │ 1.9 s │ 0 │ │ 8 │ 24 │ 540.0 │ 5.68× │ 70.0 │ 1.83 s │ 2.6 s │ 0 │ └──────┴──────┴───────────┴─────────┴───────────┴──────────┴─────────┴────────┘ On a non-batching setup, aggregate throughput stays flat while latency climbs — which is itself a useful thing to see. Add --json FILE to export. What can my machine run? Before benchmarking, local_bench fit captures your hardware (RAM, CPU, GPU/VRAM, Apple unified memory) and checks a catalog of ~50 popular models — SmolLM2, Qwen2.5, Llama 3.x, Gemma 2, Phi-3.5/4, Mistral/Mixtral, DeepSeek-R1, CodeLlama, Yi, Command-R, and more, from 135M up to 141B — against your memory budget, showing which fit and at what quantization: local_bench fit # what fits, at the best quant local_bench fit --all # include models that don't fit local_bench fit --context 8192 # budget a larger KV cache local_bench fit --quant Q4_K_M # evaluate a specific quant local_bench fit --vram 24 # what-if: "if I had a 24 GB GPU…" local_bench fit --catalog my.json # add your own models to the catalog Live list from HuggingFace Instead of the built-in catalog, pull the currently most popular models straight from the HuggingFace Hub — their parameter counts (from safetensors metadata) are sized against your hardware in real time: local_bench fit --online # top 50 text-generation models by downloads local_bench fit --online --top 100 # cast a wider net local_bench fit --online --sort trending # or: likes local_bench fit --online --refresh # bypass the 1-day cache Results are cached under $LOCAL_BENCH_HOME (~/.local_bench), so repeat runs are fast and work offline; if the Hub is unreachable, local_bench falls back to the cache (or the built-in catalog). The built-in catalog also ships each model's Ollama tag (ollama pull …) and HuggingFace repo (which LM Studio and vLLM pull from). Add your own with a JSON catalog (see examples/models.example.json): a list of {name, params_b, family?, ollama?, hf?}. Sizes are estimates (weights + KV cache + overhead), so treat "fits"/"tight" as guidance. Add --json FILE to export the hardware profile and results. Energy On a laptop, joules per token is often the number that actually decides a model: two models at the same tok/s can differ several-fold in power draw, which is the difference between one you can leave running on battery and one you can't. local_bench --energy # J/token alongside tok/s and quality local_bench --energy --full --md out.md Platform Meter Covers macOS powermetrics CPU + GPU + ANE package Linux powercap RAPL (/sys/class/powercap) CPU package only Both meters need root, so --energy is off by default and reports why it is unavailable rather than showing an empty column after a full run. The recommended setup grants passwordless access to only the power meter, so local_bench itself keeps running as you: # sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/local_bench your-username ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/powermetrics local_bench --energy # no sudo on local_bench itself local_bench --energy prints the exact line to add, with your username and the resolved binary path filled in. Running the whole tool under sudo also works, but whether $HOME is preserved depends on your sudo configuration — so run history and the response cache may land in root's home, or become root-owned files in yours. If you go that route, be explicit: sudo LOCAL_BENCH_HOME="$HOME/.local_bench" local_bench --energy How the number is derived. Neither macOS nor Linux exposes per-process energy, so the meters read whole-system power. local_bench measures idle draw once per run and subtracts it, giving a net figure attributable to inference: joules_net = (mean_watts − baseline_watts) × sampled_seconds J/token = joules_net ÷ output_tokens The Markdown report shows net and gross joules, mean watts, and the baseline that was subtracted, so you can see how much of the total was overhead. Keep the machine otherwise idle for a clean baseline. Limitations local_bench is a fast, local first look — not a rigorous benchmark of record. Keep these in mind: Quality is a signal, not a leaderboard of record. The suite is small and English-only (8 tasks in the fast default, 31 with --full); it's designed to separate your models, not to rank them authoritatively. For serious evals use lm-evaluation-harness. The optional LLM-as-judge is noisy, especially with small local judges. Speed is your-machine-at-that-moment. tok/s and TTFT depend on current load, thermal state, and memory pressure — a busy laptop (or swapping when low on RAM) will read slower. Numbers are meaningful relative to each other on the same run, not as absolute model specs. Memory is best-effort. It uses the runner's resident size where exposed (Ollama /api/ps, LM Studio /api/v0) plus RSS sampling; on unified-memory Macs it's approximate, and client-timed for OpenAI-compatible backends. fit sizes are estimates (weights + KV cache + overhead) — treat "fits/tight" as guidance, not a guarantee. HuggingFace param counts come from safetensors metadata, which is missing for GGUF-only or gated repos. Throughput scaling only appears on batching servers (vLLM, etc.); a single local model serializes requests. Energy is a whole-system estimate. The platform meters measure the machine, not the process, and Apple documents powermetrics values as model-derived estimates that "should not be used for any comparison between devices". Subtracting the idle baseline makes the numbers comparable between models in one run on one machine — nothing more. Anything else running during the probe lands in the reading, and on Linux, RAPL sees the CPU package only, so a discrete GPU's draw is missing entirely. Response caching needs a model version. Ollama reports a content digest and LM Studio reports file size and quantization, so cached answers can be tied to exact weights. A bare OpenAI-compatible endpoint reports only a model name, so those models are re-generated every run rather than risk scoring one model against another's cached answers. Development git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git cd local_bench python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e ".[dev]" pytest -q The repo ships a pre-commit config that runs gitleaks plus a few hygiene hooks, so a secret is caught before it reaches history rather than in CI after it's already there: pip install pre-commit # or: brew install pre-commit pre-commit install pre-commit run --all-files # optional: check the existing tree The codebase is small and layered: providers/ (pluggable backends), quality/ (tasks, graders, judge), metrics/ (memory sampling), runner.py (orchestration), report.py (export + tables), and tui/ + plainui.py (rendering). Adding a provider means subclassing Provider (or OpenAICompatibleProvider) and registering it; adding a task means appending to the suite in quality/tasks.py with a reference that satisfies its grader (enforced by the tests). Outside the package, tools/ holds standalone developer utilities — currently the pack viewer. They may import local_bench, never the reverse, and their dependencies are their own, so they can't weigh down an install of the CLI. Contributions welcome — new providers, task packs, and metrics especially. blocks.html_en: How quality grading works

sentences.en: How quality grading works

blocks.html_en: The suite is small on purpose — enough tasks across categories to separate models, few enough that every model runs in a couple of minutes on a laptop. Each task is graded deterministically (exact numeric match, multiple-choice letter, substring, valid-JSON, regex). Temperature is 0 and a fixed seed is used for reproducibility. See local_bench tasks for the list.

sentences.en: The suite is small on purpose — enough tasks across categories to separate models, few enough that every model runs in a couple of minutes on a laptop.
sentences.zh: 该套件有意设计得很小——足够多的跨类别任务来分离模型，数量足够少，每个模型只需几分钟就能在笔记本电脑上运行。

sentences.en: Each task is graded deterministically (exact numeric match, multiple-choice letter, substring, valid-JSON, regex).
sentences.zh: 每个任务都按确定性评分（精确数字匹配、多项选择字母、子字符串、有效 JSON、正则表达式）。

sentences.en: Temperature is 0 and a fixed seed is used for reproducibility.
sentences.zh: 温度为 0，并使用固定种子来实现再现性。

sentences.en: See local_bench tasks for the list.
sentences.zh: 请参阅 local_bench 任务以获取列表。

blocks.html_en: The optional --judge MODEL flag turns on an LLM-as-judge (any local model) that scores open-ended tasks 1–5 against a reference answer. It's a signal, not an oracle.

sentences.zh: 可选的 --judge MODEL 标志打开 LLM 作为法官（任何本地模型），根据参考答案对开放式任务进行 1-5 分评分。

sentences.en: It's a signal, not an oracle.
sentences.zh: 这是一个信号，而不是神谕。

blocks.html_en: • Every deterministic task's reference must pass its own grader. The reference is the worked example of a correct answer; if it can't clear the grader, nothing can, and the resulting 0 looks like a model failure rather than an authoring one.

blocks.html_en: • max_tokens must have headroom. The budget covers the whole reply. With exact_number — which reads the last number — a model that reaches the right answer and then keeps talking gets cut off mid-sentence and scored on whatever number landed last. Ask for the answer last, and say to stop there.

content_html_zh:
将您已有的本地法学硕士（速度、内存、精力和质量）作为实时终端排行榜进行基准测试。

local_bench 是一个单命令 TUI，它可以发现本地运行器（Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp、vLLM 或任何 OpenAI 兼容服务器）中安装的模型，运行精选的质量套件，测量令牌/秒、首次令牌时间、内存占用以及实际计算机上每个令牌的可选焦耳数，并呈现实时比较排行榜。

git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git
cd local_bench
pip install .
local_bench

就是这样。 无需配置，无需 API 密钥，无需云。

Why

有很多很好的工具可以解决这个问题的一半，但没有本地优先可以同时解决这两个问题：

  • llama-bench（在 llama.cpp 内）仅测量速度。
  • lm-evaluation-harness 衡量质量，但没有完善的笔记本电脑用户体验，并且不是围绕大多数人在本地实际使用的模型运行程序构建的。

local_bench 填补了空白：本地优先、零配置、用户体验驱动。 克隆并运行，将其指向您已经拉取的模型，并获得“我的本地模型中的哪个实际上很好，以及在这台笔记本电脑上的速度有多快？”的概览答案。

它衡量什么

公制 How
tok/s 产出代币 ÷ 生成时间。 Ollama 报告服务器端评估时间；兼容 OpenAI 的后端通过令牌流在客户端进行计时。 不包括提示处理和模型加载。
TTFT 第一个流式令牌的挂钟时间（减去运行程序报告的模型加载时间）。
记忆 运行程序公开模型时的驻留模型大小（Ollama /api/ps、LM Studio /api/v0），以及后端进程的尽力而为的峰值 RSS 样本。
活力 每个输出令牌的焦耳数，带有 --energy。 在速度探测期间从平台功率计（macOS powermetrics、Linux RAPL）采样，减去每次运行测量一次的空闲基线。 需要 root — 请参阅能量。
质量 31 项确定性分级任务，涉及数学、推理、事实回忆、指令遵循/结构化输出、提取和代码理解。 可选的法学硕士作为法官添加开放式任务（摘要、电子邮件、俳句、解释）。

安装

未发布到包索引 - 从克隆安装：

git clone https://github.com/SupermodularAI/local_bench.git
cd local_bench
pip install .                  # then run:  local_bench

更愿意将其隔离？ 首先创建一个 virtualenv，或者从同一目录使用 pipx 安装：

pipx install .

可选的附加功能（全部以相同的方式从克隆安装）：

Extra Adds
pip install '.[yaml]' YAML 任务包（JSON 包无需它即可工作）
pip install '.[anthropic]' 人择提供者，克劳德作为法官
pip install -e '.[dev]' 可编辑安装加上测试依赖项

需要 Python 3.9+。

Usage

local_bench                        # fast default: 3 smallest models, quick suite (TUI)
local_bench --all                  # benchmark every discovered model
local_bench --full                 # run the full quality suite (not just the fast subset)
local_bench --no-tui               # plain live renderer (great for piping / CI)
local_bench -m llama3.2,qwen3:8b   # only these models
local_bench --limit 3              # cap the number of models
local_bench --provider lmstudio    # use LM Studio instead of auto-detect
local_bench --provider llamacpp    # llama.cpp server (llama-server)
local_bench --provider vllm        # vLLM
local_bench --provider openai --host http://localhost:5000   # any OpenAI-compatible server
local_bench --refresh-cache        # recompute instead of reusing cached responses
local_bench --energy               # also measure joules per token (see Energy)
local_bench --no-quality           # speed + memory only (fast)
local_bench --no-speed             # quality only
local_bench --judge qwen3:8b       # enable LLM-as-judge (adds open-ended tasks)
local_bench --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://gateway  # judge off-box
local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml    # use a custom task pack instead of the built-in suite
local_bench --only math            # run one category, or name task ids
local_bench --num-ctx 16384        # raise the context window (needed for long prompts)
local_bench --add-tasks mypack.yaml  # add a pack on top of the built-in suite
local_bench --label "before tuning"  # tag this run for later diffing
local_bench --md results.md        # also export a Markdown report
local_bench --json results.json    # also export raw JSON

local_bench list                   # just list discovered models
local_bench tasks                  # show the quality suite (add --tasks to preview a pack)
local_bench history                # list past runs (saved automatically)
local_bench diff                   # diff the two most recent runs
local_bench diff 3 1               # diff run #3 (base) against run #1 (newer)
local_bench throughput             # batch-throughput sweep (concurrency 1,2,4,8)
local_bench throughput --concurrency 1,8,16 --provider vllm
local_bench fit                    # which popular models fit YOUR hardware?

运行 local_bench --help 以获取完整的标志列表。

供应商

必须至少可以联系到一名本地模特跑步者：

提供者 --提供者 默认主机 咳嗽环境为 Notes
成为 成为 http://本地主机:11434 OLLAMA_HOST 原生API；通过 /api/ps 报告模型内存。

vLLM vllm http://本地主机:8000 VLLM_HOST 如果以 --api-key 启动，则设置 VLLM_API_KEY。

自动检测尝试 Ollama → LM Studio → llama.cpp → vLLM（通用​​ openai 提供程序是显式的）。 强制使用 --provider 之一。 使用 --host 或上面的环境变量覆盖主机。

质量分级如何运作

该套件有意设计得很小——足够多的跨类别任务来分离模型，数量足够少，每个模型只需几分钟就能在笔记本电脑上运行。 每个任务都按确定性评分（精确数字匹配、多项选择字母、子字符串、有效 JSON、正则表达式）。 温度为 0，并使用固定种子来实现再现性。 请参阅 local_bench 任务以获取列表。

可选的 --judge MODEL 标志打开 LLM 作为法官（任何本地模型），根据参考答案对开放式任务进行 1-5 分评分。 这是一个信号，而不是神谕。

默认情况下很快

在笔记本电脑上对全套套件中的每个模型进行基准测试需要一段时间，因此默认值经过调整以便快速浏览：

  • 默认情况下有 3 个最小的模型（首先是最小的，所以结果显示得很快） — — 所有的一切，-m 来选择。
  • 快速质量子集（涵盖所有类别的约 8 项任务）——全部 31 项。
  • 响应缓存：质量运行使用温度 0 + 固定种子，因此响应是确定性的并缓存在 ~/.local_bench 下。 重新运行仅重新生成新的模型/任务（未更改的模型/任务会在毫秒内从缓存中重新分级）； --refresh-cache 强制重新计算，--no-cache 禁用它。

在实践中，这将第一次运行从约 15-25 分钟（所有型号、全套）变成约 1-2 分钟，重新运行只需几秒钟。 要彻底通过（CI、最终数字），请使用 local_bench --all --full。

自定义任务包

使用 JSON 或 YAML 包带来您自己的评估 - 不需要 Python。 --tasks 取代内置套件； --add-tasks 附加到它后面。 YAML 需要可选的额外选项 (pip install ".[yaml]")； JSON 开箱即用。

# mypack.yaml  —  local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml
name: my-pack
tasks:
  - id: capital_japan
    category: factual
    prompt: "What is the capital of Japan? Answer with just the city name."
    grader: {type: contains_any, values: ["Tokyo"]}
    reference: Tokyo
  - id: add
    category: math
    prompt: "What is 12 + 30? End with the answer on its own line."
    grader: {type: exact_number, value: 42}
  - id: explain          # no grader -> open-ended, scored only with --judge
    category: open
    prompt: "Explain photosynthesis in one sentence."
    reference: "Plants convert sunlight, water, and CO2 into glucose and oxygen."

Grader 类型值：exact_number (value, tol)、multiple_choice (value)、 contains_any (values)、regex (pattern、ignorecase)、valid_json (keys)、valid_json_array (length)。 对于仅限法官的任务，省略评分者。 使用 local_bench 任务 --tasks mypack.yaml 预览任何包。

example/ 中提供了两个可运行的包：sample_pack.yaml 是一个包含 4 个任务的格式，extended_pa​​ck.yaml 是一个包含 21 个任务的模板，涵盖每个类别和每个评分者类型 - 复制它并交换到您自己的提示中。

有两条规则使包装保持诚实，这两条规则都是通过对已发货的包装进行测试来强制执行的：

  • 每个确定性任务的参考都必须通过其自己的评分器。 参考文献是正确答案的实际示例；如果它无法清除分级器，则没有任何方法可以清除，并且生成的 0 看起来像是模型失败而不是创作失败。
  • max_tokens 必须有空间。 预算涵盖了整个答复。 使用exact_number（读取最后一个数字）时，模型会得到正确的答案，然后继续说话，该模型会在句子中被切断，并根据最后出现的数字进行评分。 最后询问答案，并说到此为止。

在运行包之前检查它

local_bench jobs --tasks mypack.yaml 将包打印到终端。 对于较大的，还有一个小型浏览器 UI，tools/pack_viewer，它显示将判断它的确切分级器规范旁边的每个任务，根据模型实际加载的上下文窗口绘制提示大小的图表，并将上述两个规则应用到您的包中 - 使用自己的分级器重新分级每个参考，并标记将溢出上下文的提示：

pip install -r tools/pack_viewer/requirements.txt
streamlit run tools/pack_viewer/app.py -- mypack.yaml

一个独立的实用程序而不是包的一部分：src/ 中没有任何内容导入它，并且 Streamlit 不包含 local_bench 自己的依赖项。

与不同的提供商进行判断

默认情况下，判断器与被测模型运行在同一提供者上，因此它只能是提供者服务的模型。 对于一名当地的跑步者来说，这通常意味着评委也是一名候选人——然后它会在开放式任务中给出自己的答案。 --judge-provider 和 --judge-host 将法官指向其他地方：

local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml \
  --judge <model-your-gateway-serves> \
  --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://your-gateway

openai 是有线协议，而不是供应商。 任何与 OpenAI 兼容的网关都可以工作 - LiteLLM、vLLM、Jan、LocalAI、TGI - 并且判断者是您传递给 --judge 的任何模型，来自其背后的任何提供商。 这是对小型本地模型与有能力的托管模型进行评级的方法。

克劳德饰演法官

Anthropic 的 API 与 OpenAI 不兼容 — api.anthropic.com 上没有 /v1/chat/completions — 因此 --judge-provider openai 无法直接访问它。 使用专用提供程序，它通过官方 SDK 与消息 API 进行通信：

pip install '.[anthropic]'
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-…

local_bench --judge claude-opus-5 --judge-provider anthropic

--judge 采用任何 Claude 模型 ID（claude-opus-5、claude-sonnet-5、claude-haiku-4-5）； Opus 是让评委下台的最有力也是最常见的理由。 三个请求参数没有 Anthropic 等效项，而是被处理而不是通过：温度被当前的 Claude 模型拒绝，因此被丢弃（并且该后端的响应缓存关闭，因为无法保证确定性），--num-ctx 是固定的服务器端并被报告为被忽略，并且思维被禁用，除非你通过 --think — 如果继续，它将花费法官的小令牌预算推理并且不返回任何分数。

您仍然可以使用 --judge-provider openai --judge-host 通过网关路由 Claude ... 如果您已经运行了一个；不同之处在于人择提供者不需要网关。

API 密钥

键是从环境中读取的，并且变量不必携带供应商的名称：

Order 多变的
1 无论您使用 --judge-api-key-env 命名（或 --api-key-env 对于测试中的模型）
2 $LOCAL_BENCH_JUDGE_API_KEY / $LOCAL_BENCH_API_KEY
3 提供商自己的（ANTHROPIC_API_KEY、OPENAI_API_KEY、VLLM_API_KEY，...）

对于 Anthropic 提供程序，未设置 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY 并不一定意味着没有凭据：如果没有设置上述任何一项，SDK 将回退到 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN，然后从 ant auth 登录到配置文件。

LITELLM_KEY=sk-… local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml --judge <model> \
  --judge-provider openai --judge-host https://litellm.internal \
  --judge-api-key-env LITELLM_KEY

local_bench 会警告法官是否也是基准测试模型之一，如果法官端点无法到达，则会出现错误而不是继续进行 - 无法到达的法官会给每个开放式任务打 0 分，这看起来与一致的糟糕写作相同。

长提示：set --num-ctx

如果你的包有很长的提示——多文件差异、成绩单、日志——请打开上下文窗口，或者你可能会对截断而不是模型进行评分：

local_bench --tasks mypack.yaml --num-ctx 16384

默认情况下，Ollama 以 4096 个令牌加载模型，无论模型本身支持什么（Gemma 3 宣传 131072，但仍然以 4096 加载）。 不被拒绝且不出错的提示过去 — Ollama 丢弃上下文的较旧部分并评估其余部分。 在 0.32.3 上进行测量：4,450 个令牌的提示报告prompt_eval_count=2051，并且提示顶部所述的所有内容都消失了，因此模型从片段中自信地回答。 评分者只是记录了一个错误的答案，结果中没有任何内容表明提示从未到达。

当任务的提示 + max_tokens 看起来可能溢出默认值时，local_bench 在运行前发出警告，但它只能估计令牌计数，因此当您知道提示很长时，请显式设置 --num-ctx 。 请注意权衡：较大的上下文会保留更多的 KV 缓存，这会影响模型所需的内存 - 因此请根据提示调整其大小，而不是最大化它。

--num-ctx 仅适用于 Ollama。 OpenAI 兼容服务器在启动时修复其上下文（llama.cpp --ctx-size, vLLM --max-model-len）；如果您将其传递给其中之一，local_bench 会发出警告。

我的机器可以运行什么？

在进行基准测试之前，local_bench fit 会捕获您的硬件（RAM、CPU、GPU/VRAM、Apple 统一内存），并根据您的内存检查约 50 个流行模型的目录 - SmolLM2、Qwen2.5、Llama 3.x、Gemma 2、Phi-3.5/4、Mistral/Mixtral、DeepSeek-R1、CodeLlama、Yi、Command-R 等，从 135M 到 141B预算，显示哪些适合以及量化：

local_bench fit                    # what fits, at the best quant
local_bench fit --all              # include models that don't fit
local_bench fit --context 8192     # budget a larger KV cache
local_bench fit --quant Q4_K_M     # evaluate a specific quant
local_bench fit --vram 24          # what-if: "if I had a 24 GB GPU…"
local_bench fit --catalog my.json  # add your own models to the catalog

HuggingFace 的实时列表

直接从 HuggingFace Hub 中提取当前最流行的模型，而不是内置目录 - 它们的参数计数（来自安全张量元数据）根据您的硬件实时调整大小：

local_bench fit --online              # top 50 text-generation models by downloads
local_bench fit --online --top 100    # cast a wider net
local_bench fit --online --sort trending   # or: likes
local_bench fit --online --refresh    # bypass the 1-day cache

结果缓存在 $LOCAL_BENCH_HOME (~/.local_bench) 下，因此重复运行速度很快并且可以离线工作；如果集线器无法访问，local_bench 将回退到缓存（或内置目录）。

内置目录还附带每个型号的 Ollama 标签（ollama 拉……） 和 HuggingFace 存储库（LM Studio 和 vLLM 从中提取）。 使用 JSON 目录添加您自己的目录（请参阅示例/models.example.json）：{name, params_b, family?, ollama?, hf?} 的列表。 大小是估计值（权重 + KV 缓存 + 开销），因此请以“适合”/“紧密”作为指导。 添加 --json FILE 以导出硬件配置文件和结果。

活力

在笔记本电脑上，每个令牌的焦耳数通常是实际决定型号的数字：具有相同 tok/s 的两个型号的功耗可能相差数倍，这就是可以使用电池运行的型号和不能使用电池运行的型号之间的差异。

local_bench --energy                 # J/token alongside tok/s and quality
local_bench --energy --full --md out.md
平台 Meter 封面
macOS 功率测量 CPU+GPU+ANE封装
Linux powercap RAPL（/sys/class/powercap） 仅CPU封装

两个仪表都需要 root，因此 --energy 默认情况下处于关闭状态，并报告其不可用的原因，而不是在完整运行后显示空列。

推荐的设置仅授予对功率计的无密码访问权限，因此 local_bench 本身会在您执行以下操作时保持运行：

# sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/local_bench
your-username ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/powermetrics

local_bench --energy          # no sudo on local_bench itself

local_bench --energy 打印要添加的确切行，并填写您的用户名和解析的二进制路径。

在 sudo 下运行整个工具也可以，但是否保留 $HOME 取决于您的 sudo 配置 - 因此运行历史记录和响应缓存可能会落在 root 的主目录中，或者成为您的 root 拥有的文件。 如果你走那条路，请明确：

sudo LOCAL_BENCH_HOME="$HOME/.local_bench" local_bench --energy

数字是如何得出的。 macOS 和 Linux 都不暴露每个进程的能量，因此仪表读取的是整个系统的能量。 local_bench 每次运行测量一次空闲绘制并将其减去，给出可归因于推断的净值：

joules_net = (mean_watts − baseline_watts) × sampled_seconds
J/token    = joules_net ÷ output_tokens

Markdown 报告显示净焦耳和总焦耳、平均瓦特以及减去的基线，因此您可以看到总开销中有多少。 保持机器空闲，以获得干净的基线。

局限性

local_bench 是一个快速的、本地的第一眼——不是一个严格的记录基准。 请记住以下几点：

  • 质量是一个信号，而不是记录的排行榜。 该套件很小，并且仅提供英语（fast 默认情况下有 8 个任务，使用 --full 则有 31 个任务）；它旨在区分您的模型，而不是对它们进行权威排名。 对于严肃的评估，请使用 lm-evaluation-harness。 可选的法学硕士作为法官很吵，尤其是对于规模较小的当地法官而言。
  • 速度就是那一刻您的机器。 tok/s 和 TTFT 取决于当前负载、热状态和内存压力——繁忙的笔记本电脑（或 RAM 不足时进行交换）的读取速度会变慢。 数字在同一运行中相对于彼此有意义，而不是绝对的模型规格。
  • 记忆是尽力而为的。 它使用跑步者暴露的驻留尺寸（Ollama /api/ps、LM Studio /api/v0）加上 RSS 采样；在统一内存 Mac 上，它是近似值，并且针对 OpenAI 兼容后端进行客户端计时。
  • 适合尺寸是估计值（权重 + KV 缓存 + 开销）——将“适合/紧密”视为指导，而不是保证。 HuggingFace 参数计数来自安全张量元数据，仅 GGUF 或门控存储库缺少该元数据。
  • 吞吐量缩放仅出现在批处理服务器（vLLM等）上；单个本地模型序列化请求。
  • 能量是整个系统的估计。 平台仪表测量的是机器，而不是过程，Apple 将 powermetrics 值记录为模型导出的估计值，“不应用于设备之间的任何比较”。 减去空闲基线可以使一台机器上一次运行的模型之间的数字具有可比性 - 仅此而已。 探测期间运行的任何其他内容都会出现在读取中，并且在 Linux 上，RAPL 只能看到 CPU 包，因此完全缺少独立 GPU 的绘制。
  • 响应缓存需要模型版本。 Ollama 报告内容摘要，LM Studio 报告文件大小和量化，因此缓存的答案可以与精确的权重联系起来。 裸露的 OpenAI 兼容端点仅报告模型名称，因此每次运行都会重新生成这些模型，而不是冒险根据一个模型的缓存答案对另一个模型进行评分。
